sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2 cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin²θ.

Product to Sum Formula

sin A cos B = 1/2 [sin(A + B) + sin(A − B)]. For A = B, sin A cos A = 1/2 sin 2A.

Trigonometric Values of 15°

sin 15° = (√6 − √2)/4 and cos 15° = (√6 + √2)/4.

Triple Angle Identity for Sine

sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³ θ. This is often used in problems involving cubic trigonometric terms.</p

questions.question: If sin x = 1/2 and sin y = 2/3, then what is the value of [(6 cos² x - 4 cos⁴ x)/(18 cos² y - 27 cos⁴ y)]?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute cos² x ≡ 1 − sin² x and cos² y ≡ 1 − sin² y.

Given sin x = 1/2 ⇒ cos² x = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4

Given sin y = 2/3 ⇒ cos² y = 1 − 4/9 = 5/9

Numerator = 6(3/4) − 4(3/4)² = 18/4 − 9/4 = 9/4

Denominator = 18(5/9) − 27(5/9)² = 10 − 25/3 = 5/3

Value = (9/4) ÷ (5/3) = 27/20

**∴ The correct answer is 27/20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x = 1/2

sin y = 2/3

**Formula Used:**

cos² θ = 1 − sin² θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08b291faeeba53dfafe0663d68d048f6232279e9cbaa2f28ec46ae9356671d8a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos² x = 1 − (1/2)² = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4

⇒ cos² y = 1 − (2/3)² = 1 − 4/9 = 5/9

⇒ Numerator = 6 cos² x − 4 cos⁴ x = cos² x (6 − 4 cos² x)

⇒ Numerator = (3/4) × (6 − 4 × 3/4) = (3/4) × (6 − 3) = 9/4

⇒ Denominator = 18 cos² y − 27 cos⁴ y = 9 cos² y (2 − 3 cos² y)

⇒ Denominator = 9 × (5/9) × (2 − 3 × 5/9) = 5 × (2 − 5/3) = 5 × (1/3) = 5/3

⇒ Final Value = (9/4) ÷ (5/3) = (9/4) × (3/5) = 27/20

**∴ The correct answer is 27/20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 2 cos² θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin² θ.

Power Reduction

Expressions involving cos⁴ θ can be solved by substituting (cos² θ)² or using half-angle reduction: cos² θ = (1 + cos 2θ) / 2.</p

questions.question: What is the value of cos 15° + cos 105°?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the sum-to-product transformation formula: cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2).

The average of the angles is (105° + 15°) ÷ 2 = 60°.

The half-difference of the angles is (105° − 15°) ÷ 2 = 45°.

Result = 2 × cos 60° × cos 45° = 2 × (1/2) × (1/√2) = 1/√2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = cos 15° + cos 105°

**Formula Used:**

cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b00bad626fc0abbcd96fc34d8ab6b3b6af3aa0092db932d163006b1b3612271.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos 105° + cos 15°

⇒ 2 cos((105° + 15°)/2) cos((105° − 15°)/2)

⇒ 2 cos(120°/2) cos(90°/2)

⇒ 2 cos 60° cos 45°

⇒ 2 × (1/2) × (1/√2)

⇒ 1 × (1/√2)

⇒ 1/√2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Sum-to-Product Formulas

cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((D−C)/2) and sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2).

Values of 15° and 75°

sin 15° = cos 75° = (√3 − 1)/(2√2) and cos 15° = sin 75° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2).

Complementary and Supplementary Angles

cos(90° + θ) = −sin θ and cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.</p

questions.question: If sin (A - B) = 1/2 and cos (A + B) = 1/2, then what is the value of sin A cos A + sin² A sin B cos B + cos³ A cos B tan A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify angles: sin (A − B) = 1/2 ⇒ A − B = 30° and cos (A + B) = 1/2 ⇒ A + B = 60°.

Solve for A and B: A = (60 + 30)/2 = 45° and B = (60 − 30)/2 = 15°.

Substitute: (sin 45° cos 45°) + (sin² 45° × 1/2 sin 30°) + (cos³ 45° cos 15° tan 45°).

Calculation: 1/2 + (1/2 × 1/4) + (1/(2√2) × (√3 + 1)/(2√2)) = 1/2 + 1/8 + (√3 + 1)/8 = (4 + 1 + √3 + 1)/8 = (6 + √3)/8.

**∴ The correct answer is (6 + √3)/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: sin (A − B) = 1/2 and cos (A + B) = 1/2.

Formula used: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 60° = 1/2, sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, cos (X − Y) = cos X cos Y + sin X sin Y.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/386a6c57003e2d10912fdccfda37248c9f160429c810d3052ac5edd0d0a2a203.png] 

⇒ A − B = 30° ... (i)

⇒ A + B = 60° ... (ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): 2A = 90° ⇒ A = 45°

⇒ Subtracting (i) from (ii): 2B = 30° ⇒ B = 15°

⇒ sin A = 1/√2, cos A = 1/√2, tan A = 1

⇒ cos 15° = cos(45° − 30°) = cos 45° cos 30° + sin 45° sin 30° = (1/√2 × √3/2) + (1/√2 × 1/2) = (√3 + 1)/(2√2)

⇒ sin 15° cos 15° = 1/2 sin 30° = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4

⇒ Expression = (1/√2 × 1/√2) + (1/√2)² × (1/4) + (1/√2)³ × [(√3 + 1)/(2√2)] × 1

⇒ Expression = 1/2 + 1/8 + (√3 + 1)/(2 × 2 × 2) = 1/2 + 1/8 + (√3 + 1)/8

⇒ Expression = (4 + 1 + √3 + 1) / 8 = (6 + √3) / 8

**∴ The correct answer is (6 + √3)/8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Angle Formulas

sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B and cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.

Trigonometric Values of 15° and 75°

sin 15° = cos 75° = (√3 − 1)/(2√2) and cos 15° = sin 75° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2).

Double Angle Identity

sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, which implies sin θ cos θ = (1/2) sin 2θ.</p

questions.question: What is the value of cot (90 + 75°)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the allied angle identity: cot (90° + θ) = −tan θ.

Here, θ = 75°, so cot (90° + 75°) = −tan 75°.

The standard value for tan 75° is 2 + √3.

Substitute this value: −(2 + √3) = −2 − √3.

**∴ The correct answer is −2 − √3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** expression cot (90° + 75°)

**Formula Used:** cot (90° + θ) = −tan θ and tan (A + B) = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 − tan A × tan B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/524f562495e8f6dc92b270a67151376e232bcdff81271078ebae7296c5818202.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ cot (90° + 75°) = −tan 75°

⇒ tan 75° = tan (45° + 30°)

⇒ tan 75° = (tan 45° + tan 30°) ÷ (1 − tan 45° × tan 30°)

⇒ tan 75° = (1 + 1/√3) ÷ (1 − 1/√3)

⇒ tan 75° = (√3 + 1) ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: [(√3 + 1)(√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ tan 75° = (3 + 1 + 2√3) ÷ (3 − 1) = (4 + 2√3) ÷ 2 = 2 + √3

⇒ cot (90° + 75°) = −tan 75° = −(2 + √3) = −2 − √3

**∴ The correct answer is −2 − √3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Allied Angles Property

For angles in the form (90° ± θ) or (270° ± θ), trigonometric functions change to their co-functions: sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ cosec.

ASTC Rule

In the second quadrant (90° to 180°), only Sine and Cosecant are positive. Tangent and Cotangent are negative.

Common Trig Values

tan 75° = cot 15° = 2 + √3 | tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3.</p

questions.question: If (A + B + C) = 90°, then what is the value of sin (A / 2) sin [(180 - B - C) / 2] + cos (A / 2) sin (B + C) / 2?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use value substitution: Let A = 90°, B = 0°, and C = 0°, which satisfies the condition A + B + C = 90°.

Substitute in the expression: sin(90°/2) sin[(180° − 0° − 0°)/2] + cos(90°/2) sin[(0° + 0°)/2]

⇒ sin 45° sin 90° + cos 45° sin 0°

⇒ (1 / √2) × 1 + (1 / √2) × 0 = 1 / √2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / √2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A + B + C = 90°

**Formula Used:** sin (90° − θ) = cos θ and sin (X + Y) = sin X cos Y + cos X sin Y

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4e2ca3aa86ccb97205106fb9819a0906f2a74179a03b07bd2e9f4a9129c3ce6.png] 

⇒ Given expression: sin (A / 2) sin [(180 − (B + C)) / 2] + cos (A / 2) sin [(B + C) / 2]

⇒ sin (A / 2) sin [90° − (B + C) / 2] + cos (A / 2) sin [(B + C) / 2]

⇒ Using sin (90° − θ) = cos θ:

⇒ sin (A / 2) cos [(B + C) / 2] + cos (A / 2) sin [(B + C) / 2]

⇒ This matches the form sin X cos Y + cos X sin Y, where X = A / 2 and Y = (B + C) / 2

⇒ sin [A / 2 + (B + C) / 2] = sin [(A + B + C) / 2]

⇒ Substituting A + B + C = 90°:

⇒ sin (90° / 2) = sin 45° = 1 / √2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / √2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sine Addition Formula

The sine of the sum of two angles is given by sin(X + Y) = sin X cos Y + cos X sin Y.

Complementary Angles

Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles follow the rules: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Standard Trigonometric Values

For the angle 45°, both sin 45° and cos 45° are equal to 1 / √2.</p

questions.question: What is the value of cot (90 - x) sin⁴ (90 - x) + cot (180 - x) sin⁴ (180 - x)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply allied angle reductions: cot(90 − x) = tan x, sin(90 − x) = cos x, cot(180 − x) = −cot x, and sin(180 − x) = sin x.

Expression = tan x cos⁴ x − cot x sin⁴ x.

Convert to sin and cos: (sin x / cos x) × cos⁴ x − (cos x / sin x) × sin⁴ x = sin x cos³ x − cos x sin³ x.

Factor out common terms: sin x cos x (cos² x − sin² x) = (1/2) sin 2x × cos 2x.

Using 2 sin A cos A = sin 2A: (1/4) sin 4x.

**∴ The correct answer is (sin 4x) / 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cot (90 − x) sin⁴ (90 − x) + cot (180 − x) sin⁴ (180 − x)

**Formula Used:** Allied angles and double angle identities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67911fcaf0e35e0b9b4f580163c0921f1e6faf9b285cb2e6aaf1411cd15f9c39.png] 

⇒ Term 1: cot (90 − x) sin⁴ (90 − x) = tan x (cos x)⁴ = tan x cos⁴ x

⇒ Term 2: cot (180 − x) sin⁴ (180 − x) = (−cot x) (sin x)⁴ = −cot x sin⁴ x

⇒ Expression = tan x cos⁴ x − cot x sin⁴ x

⇒ Expression = (sin x / cos x) × cos⁴ x − (cos x / sin x) × sin⁴ x

⇒ Expression = sin x cos³ x − cos x sin³ x

⇒ Expression = sin x cos x (cos² x − sin² x)

⇒ Expression = (1/2) × (2 sin x cos x) × (cos² x − sin² x)

⇒ Expression = (1/2) sin 2x cos 2x

⇒ Expression = (1/4) (2 sin 2x cos 2x) = (1/4) sin 4x

**∴ The correct answer is (sin 4x) / 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Allied Angle Relations

Trigonometric ratios change when using (90 ± θ) or (270 ± θ), where sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, and sec ↔ cosec. Ratios remain the same for (180 ± θ) or (360 ± θ), only the sign changes based on the quadrant.

Double and Multiple Angle Identities

Key formulas include sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 2 cos² θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin² θ. These allow reducing powers and expanding compound angles like sin 4x.

Fundamental Identities

Recall that sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ. These are essential for simplifying rational trigonometric expressions.</p

questions.question: A flag of height 4 metres is standing on the top of a building. The angle of elevation of the top of the flag from a point X is 45° and the angle of elevation of the top of building from X is 30°. Point X is on the ground level. What is the height (in metres) of the building?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using trigonometry ratios: For 30°, height : base = 1 : √3. For 45°, total height : base = 1 : 1.

To keep the base constant, total height : base = √3 : √3.

Flag height = Total height − Building height = (√3 − 1) units.

Given: (√3 − 1) units = 4 m ⇒ 1 unit (Building height) = 4 ÷ (√3 − 1).

On rationalizing: 4(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 2(√3 + 1) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 2(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the height of the building be H and the distance from point X to the building base be D.

Given: Flag height = 4 m. Total height of (Building + Flag) = H + 4.

Angle of elevation to top of building = 30°. Angle of elevation to top of flag = 45°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de5ea0516654576806147c0ae280e55fb6c036d7c6077f5a93f1d79951c52125.png] 

In triangle formed by building top and X:

⇒ tan 30° = H ÷ D

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = H ÷ D

⇒ D = H√3 --- (Equation 1)

In triangle formed by flag top and X:

⇒ tan 45° = (H + 4) ÷ D

⇒ 1 = (H + 4) ÷ D

⇒ D = H + 4 --- (Equation 2)

Equating D from both equations:

⇒ H√3 = H + 4

⇒ H√3 − H = 4

⇒ H(√3 − 1) = 4

⇒ H = 4 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ H = [4 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ H = [4(√3 + 1)] ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ H = 4(√3 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ H = 2(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 2(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base. Standard values include tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation

The angle between the horizontal line of sight and the line from the observer's eye to some object above the horizontal level.

Rationalization

To remove the radical from the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator: (a − √b) conjugate is (a + √b).</p

questions.question: Height of a tower is 120 metres. The angle of elevation of the top of tower from a point B is 75°. Point B is on the ground level. What is the distance (in metres) of point B from the base of tower?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between Height (h) and Distance from base (d) is given by d = h × cot θ.

Given: h = 120 m and θ = 75°.

Standard value: cot 75° = tan 15° = 2 − √3.

Substituting the values: d = 120 × (2 − √3) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 (2 − √3) m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Height of tower (AC) = 120 m, Angle of elevation at point B = 75°.

Formula Used: tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e58cb9e5350d31e47c440ad2a9a07ca5489cb52604c17feb0052342dbda99532.png] 

⇒ tan 75° = 120 / BC

⇒ BC = 120 / tan 75°

⇒ tan 75° = tan(45° + 30°) = (tan 45° + tan 30°) / (1 − tan 45° × tan 30°)

⇒ tan 75° = (1 + 1/√3) / (1 − 1/√3) = (√3 + 1) / (√3 − 1) = 2 + √3

⇒ BC = 120 / (2 + √3)

⇒ BC = [120 / (2 + √3)] × [(2 − √3) / (2 − √3)]

⇒ BC = 120(2 − √3) / (4 − 3) = 120(2 − √3)

**∴ The correct answer is 120 (2 − √3) m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Values for 15° and 75°

tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3 and tan 75° = cot 15° = 2 + √3.

Height and Distance Relation

For an angle of elevation θ, Distance = Height / tan θ. For θ = 45°, Height = Distance.

Rationalization Rule

To rationalize 1/(a + √b), multiply numerator and denominator by (a − √b) to use the identity (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b².</p

questions.question: Mohit is standing at some distance from a 60 meters tall building. Mohit is 1.8 meters tall. When Mohit walks towards the building, then the angle of elevation from his head becomes 60° from 45°. How much distance (in metres) Mohit covered towards the building?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height above Mohit's eye level (h) = 60 − 1.8 = 58.2 m.

Distance covered (d) = h × (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂), where θ₁ = 45° and θ₂ = 60°.

d = 58.2 × (cot 45° − cot 60°) = 58.2 × (1 − 1/√3).

d = 58.2 − (58.2/√3) = 19.4 × 3 − 19.4√3.

d = 19.4 (3 − √3) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.4 (3 − √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of building (H) = 60 m

Height of Mohit (hₘ) = 1.8 m

Initial angle (θ₁) = 45° and Final angle (θ₂) = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b50fce511208691b29276b42d384b5a5f40ad9914b3054b6af8518c8c65921e0.png] 

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective height (AB) = Total height − Mohit height = 60 − 1.8 = 58.2 m

⇒ In first position (45°), let base distance be x: tan 45° = 58.2 / x

⇒ 1 = 58.2 / x ⇒ x = 58.2 m

⇒ In second position (60°), let base distance be y: tan 60° = 58.2 / y

⇒ √3 = 58.2 / y ⇒ y = 58.2 / √3 = (58.2 × √3) / 3 = 19.4√3 m

⇒ Distance covered = x − y = 58.2 − 19.4√3 m

⇒ Distance covered = 19.4 (3 − √3) m

**∴ The correct answer is 19.4 (3 − √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for Heights

tan 45° = 1 and tan 60° = √3. These are the most common values used in height and distance problems.

General Formula for Distance

If an observer moves towards an object and the angle changes from α to β, the distance d = h(cot α − cot β), where h is the relative height.

Angle Observation Rule

As you move closer to a building or tower, the angle of elevation always increases (e.g., from 45° to 60°).</p

questions.question: How many litres of water should be added to a 7.5 litre mixture of acid and water containing acid and water in the ratio of 1 : 2 such that the resultant mixture has 20% acid in it?

Initial mixture = 7.5 L, Acid : Water = 1 : 2. Total units = 3.

Acid volume = (1/3) × 7.5 = 2.5 L.

New mixture requires 20% acid. Acid quantity remains constant as only water is added.

20% of New Mixture = 2.5 L ⇒ 100% of New Mixture = 2.5 × 5 = 12.5 L.

Water to be added = New Mixture − Old Mixture = 12.5 − 7.5 = 5 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Volume = 7.5 L, Initial Ratio (A:W) = 1 : 2, Final Acid % = 20%.

⇒ Ratio = 20 : 13.33 = 3 : 2

⇒ 3 units represent 7.5 L.

⇒ 1 unit = 7.5 ÷ 3 = 2.5 L.

⇒ 2 units (Water Added) = 2 × 2.5 = 5 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 litres.**

Profit Ratio = (Investment₁ × Time₁) : (Investment₂ × Time₂) : (Investment₃ × Time₃)

questions.question: Find the number of students who took an exam if the ratio of those who passed to those who failed in the exam was 10 : 3. If 40 more students had taken the exam and 10 less had failed, then the ratio of those who passed to those who failed in the exam would have been 5 : 1.

Ratio of Total : Failed = 13 : 3 (Initial) and 6 : 1 (New, as Passed : Failed = 5 : 1).

Total change = +40, Failed change = −10.

Apply Cross-Product: |(13 × 1) − (6 × 3)| units = |(6 × (−10)) − (1 × 40)|.

5 units = |−60 − 40| = 100.

1 unit = 20 ⇒ Initial Total = 13 units = 13 × 20 = 260.

**∴ The correct answer is 260 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Passed : Failed = 10 : 3. New Passed : Failed = 5 : 1. Total increased by 40, Failed decreased by 10.

Let initial Passed = 10x and initial Failed = 3x.

Initial Total Students = 10x + 3x = 13x.

New Total Students = 13x + 40.

New Failed Students = 3x − 10.

New Passed Students = (13x + 40) − (3x − 10) = 10x + 50.

⇒ (10x + 50) ÷ (3x − 10) = 5 ÷ 1

⇒ 10x + 50 = 5 × (3x − 10)

⇒ 10x + 50 = 15x − 50

⇒ 15x − 10x = 50 + 50

⇒ 5x = 100

⇒ x = 20

⇒ Initial Students = 13x = 13 × 20 = 260.

Componendo and Dividendo

questions.question: A zoo has an average of 500 visitors on Sundays and 200 on other days. The average number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days beginning with a Sunday is:

questions.question: A bank gives Rs. 25,000 on a saving a certain principal in 2 years at 8% rate of interest. How much will the bank give (in Rs.) on the same principal in 4 years at the same rate of interest compounded annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the rate is constant, the Amount grows geometrically: A₄ = A₂ × (1 + r/100)⁽⁴⁻²⁾.

Given Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹25,000 and Rate (r) = 8%.

Amount after 4 years (A₄) = 25000 × (1 + 8/100)²

⇒ A₄ = 25000 × (1.08) × (1.08) = 25000 × 1.1664

⇒ A₄ = 29160.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹25,000

Rate of Interest (r) = 8% p.a.

Time (t) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a56b92d9d9c4724cb154378ec1f67c1e74f0c8751f7b4d2b58dbc57f54a932cc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₂ = P(1 + 8/100)² = 25000

⇒ A₄ = P(1 + 8/100)⁴

⇒ Dividing A₄ by A₂:

⇒ A₄ ÷ A₂ = [P(1 + 8/100)⁴] ÷ [P(1 + 8/100)²]

⇒ A₄ / 25000 = (1 + 8/100)²

⇒ A₄ / 25000 = (108 / 100) × (108 / 100)

⇒ A₄ / 25000 = (27 / 25) × (27 / 25)

⇒ A₄ = 25000 × (729 / 625)

⇒ A₄ = 40 × 729

⇒ A₄ = 29160

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years at r%, the effective compound interest rate is (r + r + r²/100)%.

Geometric Progression in CI

In compound interest, amounts at equal intervals of time (t, 2t, 3t...) form a Geometric Progression (G.P.).

Amount Relation

If Aₙ is the amount after n years, then A₂ₙ / Aₙ = Aₙ / P = (1 + r/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: Find the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3 years is Rs. 900 and compound interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 636?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest (SI) for 1 year = 900 ÷ 3 = ₹300.

SI for 2 years = 300 × 2 = ₹600.

Difference (Interest on Interest) for 2 years = 636 − 600 = ₹36.

Rate of Interest (R) = (36 ÷ 300) × 100 = 12%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) for 3 years = ₹900, Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹636.

**Formula Used:** Rate (R) = [(CI₂ yₑₐᵣₛ − SI₂ yₑₐᵣₛ) ÷ (SI for 1 year)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/feda303b1a0e1ca1fea994a1f811d2977a7ae501e712bcabe59f107e25896425.png] 

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) for 1 year = 900 ÷ 3 = ₹300

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = 300 × 2 = ₹600

⇒ Difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years = 636 − 600 = ₹36

⇒ This difference ₹36 is the interest calculated on the 1st year's SI of ₹300.

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = (36 ÷ 300) × 100

⇒ R = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference D between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula: D = PR² / 100².

Effective Rate for Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as: R + R + (R × R) / 100.

Relation between CI and SI for 2 years

Compound interest and simple interest for 2 years are related as: CI = SI × (1 + R/200).
